quarterly_data.signal: Nanya's Q3 2026 investor-conference deck (unaudited): Q3'26 net sales NT$133,649 million, up 61.9% QoQ (Q2'26: NT$82,549 million) and 611.7% YoY (Q3'25: NT$18,779 million); gross margin 85.7% (Q2'26: 79.5%); operating income NT$106,894 million, operating margin 80.0% (Q2'26: 73.7%); net income NT$87,627 million, net margin 65.6%; EPS NT$25.40 (Q2'26: NT$14.66). Q1'26~Q3'26 net profit NT$163.9 billion, EPS NT$49.28. Revenue drivers QoQ: ASP increased >60% (primarily reflecting renewed long-term agreements), bit shipment decreased mid-single digit%, FX favorable low-single digit%; YoY: ASP increased >500%, shipment decreased low-single digit%.

quarterly_data.signal: Nanya deck operation update: new fab equipment move-in Q1'27; ramp to 30K WSPM by end of 2028; target up to 50K WSPM by 2030; new fabs planned generally aligned with future AI projects under LTAs. 1C CS Q1'27; 1D/1E/EUV development on track. Nanya continues to provide DDR5, LPDDR5/5X, DDR4, LPDDR4/4X, DDR3 and LPDDR3 and to support customized AI/WoW products and AI infrastructure solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: new fab equipment move-in Q1'27; 30K WSPM by end of 2028; up to 50K WSPM by 2030; 1C CS Q1'27

quarterly_data.signal: Nanya DRAM market outlook (Q4'26, company view): AI computation (GPU, TPU, CPU and ASIC) dominates DRAM demand growth, and AI drives DRAM demand beyond HBM and LPDDR5 across networking, storage and system management; memory supply to smartphones, PCs and general consumers is suppressed; suppliers' long-term capacity is planned based on LTA commitments; new fab construction, equipment delivery and process-node introduction all require longer lead time; lean supply-side inventory; in general applications the supply shortage and higher ASP result in down-specification or extended lifecycles, with recycled DRAM partially supporting the low-end market.
